findings.description: The prohibited-pattern checklist bans direct `new ...Service(...)` construction for DI-target classes. `AiConsultationService` is a Spring `@Service`, but the unit test constructs it directly in three test cases. findings.evidence: Package is `com.skishop.service` at line 1, while the class is annotated `@Repository` at line 20 and contains JDBC upsert SQL from line 25 onward.

findings.description: AGENTS.md targets both line and branch coverage at 80% or higher. The POM configures JaCoCo `prepare-agent` and `report`, but has no `check` execution with LINE and BRANCH minimums, so builds can pass below the stated quality bar.

findings.suggestedFix: Add a JaCoCo `check` execution in `verify` with LINE and BRANCH covered-ratio minimums of `0.80`, or document why the module is temporarily exempt.

results.summary: DDD domain review found no child-entity repository violations, but the implementation has High-severity issues: inter-aggregate coordination is done by direct service calls, PostgreSQL upsert SQL bypasses aggregate/domain policy behavior, and monetary concepts are not modeled as immutable value objects.

findings.title: Zero-hit recording is coupled by direct service-to-service call instead of a domain event
findings.description: `ProductSearchService.search` runs in a transaction and directly calls `ZeroHitRecordingService.record` when a product search has zero results. From a DDD perspective, product search and zero-hit demand recording are separate aggregate/use-case concerns; the coordination should be expressed as a domain event such as `ProductSearchReturnedZeroResultsEvent` / `ZeroHitDetectedEvent` and handled by an event listener. No `ApplicationEventPublisher` usage exists in the target code.
findings.evidence: `if (!trimmedKeyword.isBlank() && totalCount == 0) { zeroHitRecordingService.record(trimmedKeyword); ... }`; repository-wide search found no `ApplicationEventPublisher`, `publishEvent`, `@EventListener`, or `@TransactionalEventListener`.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce an immutable record event carrying the normalized/display keyword and occurred time, publish it from the product search use case via `ApplicationEventPublisher`, and handle recording in a dedicated listener. If recording must occur after the search transaction commits, use `@TransactionalEventListener(phase = AFTER_COMMIT)`.

findings.title: Native upsert bypasses ZeroHitSearch aggregate behavior and duplicates domain rules in SQL
findings.description: `ZeroHitAtomicUpsertGateway` mutates `zero_hit_searches` directly using SQL for `hit_count`, `priority`, and `estimated_opportunity_loss`. This bypasses `ZeroHitSearch.firstHit` / `recordRepeat` and `ZeroHitDemandPolicy`, so the production PostgreSQL path can drift from the aggregate invariants and policy implementation.
findings.evidence: The SQL sets `hit_count`, calculates `estimated_opportunity_loss`, and encodes priority thresholds with `CASE WHEN ... >= 5 THEN 'HIGH' ... >= 2 THEN 'MEDIUM'`. The same rules also exist in `ZeroHitSearch.priorityFor` and `ZeroHitDemandPolicy`.
findings.suggestedFix: Move mutation back through the aggregate, for example by using a locked repository method (`findByNormalizedKeyword` with pessimistic write lock) plus `ZeroHitSearch.firstHit` / `recordRepeat` inside one transaction, with unique-constraint retry for concurrent inserts. If native upsert must remain, isolate it as infrastructure and add strong tests/guards proving it cannot diverge from the aggregate policy.

findings.title: Money-like concepts are raw BigDecimal fields instead of immutable value objects
findings.description: `Product.price` and `ZeroHitSearch.estimatedOpportunityLoss` are core monetary domain values but are modeled as bare `BigDecimal` fields. The DDD checklist requires value objects such as Money to be immutable Java records with self-validation and JPA embedding/conversion. As implemented, currency/scale/non-negative invariants are not centralized in a value object.
findings.evidence: `Product` declares `private BigDecimal price`; `ZeroHitSearch` declares `private BigDecimal estimatedOpportunityLoss` at `src/main/java/com/skishop/entity/ZeroHitSearch.java:40`. No `@Embeddable`, `@Embedded`, or `Money` type exists in the reviewed source.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a `Money` value object record with compact-constructor validation for amount, currency, scale, and non-negativity, then persist it via `@Embedded`/converter according to the chosen JPA mapping. Use it for product price and estimated opportunity loss while keeping DTOs frontend-friendly if needed.

findings.title: Product aggregate does not enforce its own domain invariants
findings.description: `Product` is effectively a read-only data holder with getters and lifecycle timestamps. Its constructor accepts blank manufacturer/name/category/description and any non-null `BigDecimal` price, while the database migration carries the non-negative price check. Aggregate invariants should be protected in the domain model, not only in schema constraints or seed-data assumptions.
findings.evidence: The constructor assigns core fields using only `Objects.requireNonNull(...)`; it does not reject blank business text or negative price. The DB check `chk_products_price_non_negative` exists in `src/main/resources/db/migration/V1__create_products_and_zero_hit_searches.sql:13`, showing the invariant exists but is not enforced by the aggregate.
findings.suggestedFix: Add domain-level validation in the Product constructor/factory, preferably through value objects such as `ProductName`, `CategoryName`, and `Money`, or at minimum local `requireText` and non-negative price checks.

escalations.description: Decide whether zero-hit recording must remain synchronously reflected in the search API response (`zeroHitRecorded=true`) or can become eventually consistent through a domain event listener. That product/API decision affects the correct transaction phase for the event handler.

designDeviations.description: Inter-aggregate coordination is implemented with direct service calls rather than domain events via `ApplicationEventPublisher`.
Money-like domain values are not implemented as immutable value objects and are not embedded/converted consistently in entities.

results.summary: Reviewed the full backend from the API endpoint perspective. No legacy .do mappings were found and the implemented URLs match the documented /api contract, but there are High-severity endpoint design gaps: GET search performs a write, and API errors use a custom payload rather than Spring ProblemDetail/RFC 9457.

findings.title: GET /api/products/search records zero-hit demand as a side effect
findings.description: The search endpoint is mapped as GET, but the request path can persist or update a zero-hit record when the search has no results. This violates HTTP safe-method semantics and makes crawlers, retries, caches, and prefetches capable of mutating demand metrics.
findings.evidence: ProductController exposes @GetMapping("/search"). ProductSearchService.search is @Transactional and calls zeroHitRecordingService.record(trimmedKeyword) when totalCount == 0 at src/main/java/com/skishop/service/ProductSearchService.java:44 and :63-65.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep GET /api/products/search read-only. Move zero-hit recording to an explicit POST endpoint such as POST /api/zero-hit-searches or POST /api/products/search-events with a validated request DTO, then update the frontend and design docs together.

findings.title: API errors do not use Spring ProblemDetail / RFC 9457 format
findings.description: GlobalExceptionHandler and ApiErrorWriter return the project-specific ApiErrorResponse record instead of Spring Boot 3.2 ProblemDetail and do not extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler. This misses the review standard for RFC 9457-compatible error responses, even though stack trace exposure is correctly disabled in application.yml.
findings.evidence: @RestControllerAdvice public class GlobalExceptionHandler returns ResponseEntity<ApiErrorResponse>; build() creates new ApiErrorResponse at lines 125-132. ApiErrorResponse is a custom record at src/main/java/com/skishop/exception/ApiErrorResponse.java:16-23, and ApiErrorWriter writes the same custom payload at src/main/java/com/skishop/exception/ApiErrorWriter.java:36-41.
findings.suggestedFix: Extend ResponseEntityExceptionHandler where appropriate and return ProblemDetail, e.g. ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(status, message), with stable extension properties such as code, path, and errors. Align the security ApiErrorWriter with the same ProblemDetail shape.

findings.title: Current-user endpoint manually casts Authentication instead of using @AuthenticationPrincipal
findings.description: GET /api/auth/me obtains the principal from Authentication and casts it manually. The endpoint is protected by SecurityConfig, so the immediate risk is limited, but it does not follow the project review convention for current-user resource access and can become brittle if another Authentication implementation reaches the controller.
findings.evidence: public AuthMeResponse me(Authentication authentication) { AdminUserDto user = (AdminUserDto) authentication.getPrincipal(); ... }
findings.suggestedFix: Change the signature to me(@AuthenticationPrincipal AdminUserDto user) and return a controlled 401/403 if the principal is absent or unexpected. For logout, keep Authentication only if the token credential is still needed, or pass the token through a dedicated validated/security abstraction.

findings.title: LoginRequest accepts unbounded username and password strings
findings.description: LoginRequest uses @NotBlank but does not bound username or password length with @Size. Validation is executed via @Valid in AuthController, and the server has a 1MB post limit, but field-level bounds are still missing for an attacker-controlled authentication payload.
findings.evidence: public record LoginRequest(@NotBlank String username, @NotBlank String password)
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit field limits, for example @NotBlank @Size(max = 100) String username and @NotBlank @Size(min = 8, max = 256) String password, choosing bounds that match the admin credential policy and tests.

findings.title: Admin controllers inline full /api/admin paths instead of class-level base mapping
findings.description: AdminZeroHitController and AiConsultController do not define a class-level @RequestMapping base path. Their behavior is correct today, but it diverges from the controller convention requiring an appropriate base path per controller class and makes related admin endpoint mappings less uniform.
findings.evidence: AdminZeroHitController has @RestController and @Validated but no class-level @RequestMapping; the method uses @GetMapping("/api/admin/zero-hits"). AiConsultController similarly uses @PostMapping("/api/admin/ai-consult") at src/main/java/com/skishop/controller/AiConsultController.java:31 without a class-level base mapping.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @RequestMapping("/api/admin") to both admin controllers, then change method mappings to @GetMapping("/zero-hits") and @PostMapping("/ai-consult").

escalations.description: Decide whether to make zero-hit recording a breaking API change now. Fixing GET side effects requires frontend and design updates because backend-design.md currently documents GET /api/products/search as recording zero-hit demand.
Decide the migration timing for ProblemDetail because README currently documents a custom ApiErrorResponse payload while the review standard and modify plan recommend RFC 9457.

designDeviations.description: The modify plan recommends splitting zero-hit recording out of GET search and migrating errors to ProblemDetail, but the current implementation still records from GET /api/products/search and returns ApiErrorResponse.

results.summary: Async/concurrency review found 2 Critical and 2 High issues. The code has no Spring async/scheduled/future fire-and-forget patterns, but it is not virtual-thread enabled and contains synchronized blocks around JDBC/JPA I/O that would pin virtual-thread carrier threads once enabled.

findings.title: JPA read/write operations are executed inside synchronized fallback upsert lock
findings.description: `recordWithJpaFallback` enters a JVM monitor and then performs repository lookup and save operations. This path is reachable from the product search request flow when PostgreSQL-native upsert is not supported. With Java 21 virtual threads, blocking JDBC inside `synchronized` can pin carrier threads; regardless of virtual threads, it serializes all fallback zero-hit writes through one singleton lock.
findings.evidence: synchronized (fallbackUpsertLock) { return zeroHitSearchRepository.findByNormalizedKeyword(...).map(...save...).orElseGet(...save...); }
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer a database-level atomic upsert or unique-constraint retry path for every supported database. If a JVM fallback lock remains, replace monitor locking with `ReentrantLock` and keep the critical section as small as possible; avoid holding it across JDBC calls where feasible, for example by handling duplicate insert conflicts and retrying the update in a new transaction.

findings.title: Database metadata lookup occurs inside synchronized supports check
findings.description: `supportsAtomicUpsert()` uses `synchronized (this)` and calls `databaseProductName()`, which opens a JDBC connection and reads metadata. That is blocking I/O inside a monitor and can pin a virtual-thread carrier on the first concurrent request that initializes the cached value.
findings.evidence: synchronized (this) { if (atomicUpsertSupported == null) { atomicUpsertSupported = databaseProductName().contains(POSTGRESQL); } } and `databaseProductName()` calls `dataSource.getConnection()` at line 106.
findings.suggestedFix: Initialize database support outside a Java monitor, such as during bean initialization, or use `ReentrantLock`/an atomic lazy holder that does not monitor-pin while waiting on JDBC. If duplicate detection calls are acceptable, compute outside the lock and publish the volatile cached value afterward.

findings.title: Spring Boot virtual threads are not enabled
findings.description: The project targets Java 21 and uses Spring Boot 3.2.12, but neither the default nor docker configuration enables Spring virtual threads. Synchronous MVC, JPA, and Spring AI calls therefore run on platform request threads, increasing the blast radius of slow database/provider I/O.
findings.evidence: `application.yml` defines `spring.application`, datasource, JPA, Flyway, and AI settings, but no `spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true`; `application-docker.yml` also does not add it.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `spring.threads.virtual.enabled: true` to the common Spring configuration, then remove or refactor monitor-wrapped I/O before relying on it in production.

findings.title: Admin active-token limit is enforced with a non-atomic check-then-put sequence
findings.description: The session map is a `ConcurrentHashMap`, but `issueToken()` performs `enforceActiveTokenLimit(user)` and then `sessions.put(...)` as separate operations. Concurrent successful logins can all observe fewer than three active sessions and then insert, exceeding `MAX_ACTIVE_TOKENS_PER_ADMIN`. This is a compound invariant race in singleton mutable state.
findings.evidence: `issueToken` calls `enforceActiveTokenLimit(user)` before generating and inserting the token; `enforceActiveTokenLimit` counts/removes entries via streams at lines 136-146 without a shared lock around the whole mutation.
findings.suggestedFix: Guard the full token issuance invariant with a small `ReentrantLock` or synchronize only the in-memory session mutation block. Keep password verification and other potentially slow work outside the lock.

escalations.description: Decide whether the JPA zero-hit fallback is a supported runtime path or only a test/dev compatibility path. If it is supported, it needs a non-pinning, database-safe concurrency design; if not, removing it would reduce production concurrency risk.

The review fails on missing correlation ID/MDC propagation, non-RFC7807 error payloads, incomplete production log configuration, and failure logs that omit stack traces.

findings.title: No request correlation ID is assigned, propagated, or included in logs
findings.description: The request logging filter records method, path, status, and duration, but it never reads or generates `X-Correlation-Id`, never sets MDC, never returns the correlation ID response header, and there is no Logback MDC integration. This will make multi-service or even multi-request incident reconstruction unnecessarily slow.
findings.evidence: `RequestLoggingFilter` only calls `filterChain.doFilter(...)` and logs request fields in `finally`; repository-wide searches for `MDC`, `X-Correlation-Id`, and `correlationId` returned no production implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a `OncePerRequestFilter` that reads `X-Correlation-Id`, generates a UUID when absent, calls `MDC.put("correlationId", correlationId)`, sets the response header, and clears MDC in `finally`. Include `%X{correlationId}` or a JSON `correlationId` field in Logback.

findings.title: Unexpected exception logging drops the stack trace
findings.description: The global 500 handler logs only the request URI and exception class name. Without passing the exception as the final SLF4J argument, production logs will not contain the stack trace needed to diagnose the root cause.
findings.evidence: `LOGGER.error("Unexpected API error at {} with type {}", request.getRequestURI(), exception.getClass().getName());`
findings.suggestedFix: Use `LOGGER.error("Unexpected API error path={} type={}", request.getRequestURI(), exception.getClass().getName(), exception);` while keeping the client response sanitized.

findings.title: AI provider failures are caught but logged without the exception
findings.description: `AiProviderException` is converted to a fallback/error response, which is user-safe, but the catch block logs only `providerStatus`. This hides provider exception type, cause, and stack trace from operations logs during outages.
findings.evidence: `catch (AiProviderException exception) { ... LOGGER.warn("ai_consultation providerStatus={}", response.providerStatus()); }`
findings.suggestedFix: Log the throwable without prompt or credential data, for example `LOGGER.warn("ai_consultation providerStatus={} errorType={}", response.providerStatus(), exception.getClass().getName(), exception);`.

findings.title: Global exception responses do not use Spring `ProblemDetail`
findings.description: The handler is centralized and sanitized, but it returns a custom `ApiErrorResponse` record instead of Spring Boot `ProblemDetail`. This fails the review requirement for RFC 7807/RFC 9457 compatible error responses.
findings.evidence: Handler methods return `ResponseEntity<ApiErrorResponse>` and `build(...)` constructs `new ApiErrorResponse(...)`; no `ProblemDetail` usage exists in production code.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate exception handlers to return `ProblemDetail` with stable `title`, `detail`, `status`, and extension properties such as `code`, `path`, and validation `errors`. Coordinate with frontend contract tests because this is a breaking response-shape change.

findings.title: Production JSON Logback configuration is missing
findings.description: The project has SLF4J placeholder-style log calls, but no `logback-spring.xml` and no `logstash-logback-encoder` dependency were found. Production logs will remain default text logs and cannot reliably carry structured fields, correlation IDs, or trace IDs.
findings.evidence: Dependencies include actuator, web, security, validation, JPA, Flyway, Spring AI, H2/PostgreSQL, and tests, but no `net.logstash.logback:logstash-logback-encoder`. `src/main/resources` contains only `application.yml` and `application-docker.yml`.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `logstash-logback-encoder` and `src/main/resources/logback-spring.xml` with JSON output for production, including `application`, `correlationId`, and trace/span fields where available.

findings.title: Business and domain failures are mapped through broad `IllegalArgumentException` handling
findings.description: The global handler maps all `IllegalArgumentException` cases to a generic 400 `INVALID_PARAMETER`. Domain invariant failures and request parameter failures are therefore indistinguishable in logs and responses, and the required hierarchy for business, validation, not-found, authorization, and concurrency errors is incomplete.

findings.suggestedFix: Introduce explicit exceptions such as `ValidationException`, `BusinessException`, `ResourceNotFoundException`, and `ConcurrencyException`, then map them to 400/422/404/409 in the global handler. findings.description: The actuator dependency is present and health probes are configured, but web exposure includes only `health`. This limits runtime observability and does not satisfy the health plus metrics expectation in the review checklist.

results.summary: Data-access review found 2 Critical, 5 High, and 2 Medium issues. The schema is Flyway-managed, OSIV is disabled, and list queries are bounded, but the implementation deviates from the review agent's entity conventions and has transaction/timestamp risks around zero-hit persistence.

findings.title: Default profiles embed JDBC URLs instead of requiring externalized datasource configuration
findings.description: The default and docker profiles include hardcoded JDBC URL fallbacks inside environment placeholders. Under the review standard, JDBC URLs must not be hardcoded; if an environment variable is omitted, the application silently connects to a built-in location.
findings.evidence: url: ${SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL:jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/skishop}; docker profile also has jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/skishop at application-docker.yml:3.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove JDBC URL defaults from shared/runtime profiles. Require SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL, and move local/demo defaults into an explicitly activated local profile or compose-only environment.

findings.title: java.sql.Timestamp is used in the PostgreSQL upsert path
findings.description: The upsert gateway imports and binds java.sql.Timestamp even though the data-access standard prohibits java.sql.Timestamp/java.util.Date and requires java.time usage throughout date/time persistence code.
findings.evidence: import java.sql.Timestamp; and "searchedAt", Timestamp.from(searchedAt)
findings.suggestedFix: Bind a java.time value directly, or use OffsetDateTime/LocalDateTime with an explicit UTC policy. For PostgreSQL, prefer TIMESTAMPTZ plus OffsetDateTime/Instant-compatible binding instead of introducing java.sql.Timestamp in application code.

findings.title: Primary keys use UUID type and entity/JDBC generation instead of String UUID generated in the service layer
findings.description: Both entities use java.util.UUID IDs, repositories are keyed by UUID, and IDs are generated inside entity lifecycle/domain factory/JDBC code. The review standard requires String UUID primary keys and service-layer UUID.randomUUID().toString() generation, with no entity-side generation.
findings.evidence: Product.id is UUID; Product.prePersist generates UUID at lines 88-90. ZeroHitSearch.id is UUID at ZeroHitSearch.java:23-25 and generates UUID at lines 121 and 180; repositories use JpaRepository<..., UUID>.
findings.suggestedFix: Either migrate IDs to String/VARCHAR(36) and generate them in services before construction, or record an explicit project exception and update the agent standards/design docs to approve PostgreSQL UUID IDs.

findings.title: Product columns rely on implicit column names
findings.description: Product fields have @Column annotations but several omit the explicit name attribute. The standard requires every field to declare @Column(name = "snake_case") so the entity is not dependent on implicit naming strategy behavior.
findings.evidence: Examples: @Column(nullable = false, updatable = false) private UUID id; @Column(nullable = false, length = 100) private String manufacturer; @Column(nullable = false) private String name; @Column(nullable = false, precision = 12, scale = 2) private BigDecimal price.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit names such as @Column(name = "id", ...), @Column(name = "manufacturer", ...), @Column(name = "name", ...), @Column(name = "category", ...), @Column(name = "description", ...), and @Column(name = "price", ...).

findings.title: ZeroHitSearch columns rely on implicit column names
findings.description: ZeroHitSearch also omits explicit column names for fields whose Java name currently matches the database column. This violates the explicit snake_case column mapping rule and makes future naming-strategy changes risky.

results.summary: Security review found 2 Critical, 3 High, and 1 Medium issues. The highest risks are bypassable login throttling via trusted client-supplied forwarding headers and default Docker database credentials.

findings.title: Login lockout can be bypassed by spoofing X-Forwarded-For
findings.description: The login controller derives the rate-limit source IP directly from X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP before falling back to remoteAddr. Because these headers are client-controlled unless a trusted reverse proxy strips and rewrites them, an attacker can rotate X-Forwarded-For values and avoid the per-username/per-IP lockout. This materially weakens the credential-stuffing/brute-force protection on the public login endpoint.
findings.evidence: sourceIp() returns request.getHeader("X-Forwarded-For").split(",")[0].trim() before request.getRemoteAddr(); InMemoryLoginAttemptLimiter keys attempts by username + sourceIp.
findings.suggestedFix: Only trust forwarding headers when the immediate peer is a configured trusted proxy, or remove this parsing and use request.getRemoteAddr(). Prefer edge rate limiting at the reverse proxy/gateway and configure Spring's ForwardedHeaderFilter/server.forward-headers-strategy only behind a trusted proxy that strips incoming client headers.

findings.title: Docker profile ships default database credentials
findings.description: application-docker.yml falls back to literal database username/password values. If the Docker profile is deployed without overriding SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME and SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD, the service uses a predictable credential pair, which violates the repository's no-hardcoded-secret policy and creates an avoidable production misconfiguration risk.
findings.evidence: username: ${SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME:skishop}; password: ${SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD:skishop}
findings.suggestedFix: Remove secret fallbacks from runtime profiles: use username: ${SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME} and password: ${SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD}. Put demo-only values in compose/smoke files or .env.example, not in application runtime config.

findings.title: Security headers are incomplete and not explicitly configured
findings.description: The SecurityFilterChain does not configure Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, or server header suppression. Spring Security defaults cover some baseline headers, but the project standard explicitly requires these headers; missing CSP/HSTS/referrer/permissions policy leaves less defense in depth if JSON is rendered by a browser, if future HTML endpoints are added, or if bearer-token UI flows are embedded in unsafe contexts.
findings.evidence: The filter chain configures csrf/cors/session/authorization/exception handling but has no .headers(...) block; application.yml also has no server.server-header setting.
findings.suggestedFix: Add .headers(headers -> headers.contentTypeOptions(...).frameOptions(...).httpStrictTransportSecurity(...).contentSecurityPolicy(...).referrerPolicy(...).permissionsPolicy(...)) and set server.server-header to blank where supported. Confirm HSTS is enabled only when served over HTTPS or behind TLS-terminating infrastructure.

findings.category: A05/D Denial of Service - Request Size Limits
findings.title: Configured body limits do not cover JSON request bodies
findings.description: The application configures Tomcat form-post and swallow limits, but the public login endpoint and admin AI consult endpoint parse JSON @RequestBody payloads. Bean Validation size checks run after the JSON body has already been read/deserialized, and LoginRequest has no maximum length constraints. A large JSON body can consume memory and request threads before validation rejects it.
findings.evidence: server.tomcat.max-http-form-post-size: 1MB is form-specific; controllers use @RequestBody at AuthController:38 and AiConsultController:32.
findings.suggestedFix: Enforce a request Content-Length/body limit for application/json via reverse proxy, servlet filter, or container valve; return 413 for oversized bodies. Also add @Size caps to LoginRequest username/password as a secondary validation layer.

findings.category: D Denial of Service - Rate Limiter State Exhaustion
findings.title: Login attempt limiter has unbounded in-memory key growth
findings.description: The login limiter stores every failed username/source-IP combination in a ConcurrentHashMap and only removes entries on successful login. Attackers can submit many random usernames and, because source IP is header-derived, many spoofed source values to grow the map indefinitely on a public endpoint. This can become a memory exhaustion vector and also makes rate-limit behavior instance-local in multi-replica deployments.
findings.evidence: private final Map<String, AttemptState> attempts = new ConcurrentHashMap<>(); recordFailure() inserts by key(username, sourceIp); there is no max size, TTL eviction, or cleanup of expired unlocked entries.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a bounded cache with expire-after-write/access and maximumSize, or move throttling to Redis/gateway with TTL keys. Normalize and trust source IP only after fixing forwarded header handling. Add tests for eviction and high-cardinality attack behavior.

findings.title: Production code accepts {noop} admin passwords without a profile guard
findings.description: The PasswordEncoder bean uses Spring's DelegatingPasswordEncoder, which accepts the {noop} encoder. The code comment says this supports local tests, but there is no production validation rejecting {noop} in app.admin.password. A misconfigured deployment could run the admin account with a plaintext password value.
findings.evidence: passwordEncoder() returns PasswordEncoderFactories.createDelegatingPasswordEncoder(); comment explicitly mentions {noop} support for local tests.
findings.suggestedFix: Add startup validation that app.admin.password starts with {bcrypt} (or another approved adaptive encoder) outside the test profile. Keep {noop} only in test configuration or replace tests with bcrypt fixtures.

findings.title: Product listing executes an avoidable second count query
findings.description: JpaSpecificationExecutor.findAll(specification, pageable) returns a Page and already has the total-count path available. The service discards the Page, then immediately calls productRepository.count(specification), adding an extra count query to every product-list request.
findings.evidence:
List<Product> products = productRepository.findAll(specification, pageable).getContent();
long totalCount = productRepository.count(specification);
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the Page returned by findAll and use page.getTotalElements(): Page<Product> page = productRepository.findAll(specification, pageable); return new ProductListResponse(page.getContent().stream().map(productMapper::toDto).toList(), page.getTotalElements());

findings.title: Product search executes an avoidable second count query
findings.description: The search path has the same Page-discarding pattern as product listing. For common full pages, this can run a count as part of the Page creation and then run productRepository.count(specification) again before deciding whether to record a zero hit.
findings.evidence:
List<Product> products = productRepository.findAll(specification, pageable).getContent();
long totalCount = productRepository.count(specification);
findings.suggestedFix: Store Page<Product> page = productRepository.findAll(specification, pageable), map page.getContent(), and use page.getTotalElements() for both response metadata and the zero-hit decision.

findings.title: Collection APIs are capped but not truly paginated
findings.description: The public product list/search and admin zero-hit endpoints accept only limit and always request page 0. This bounds memory, but it is not real pagination: clients cannot request later pages and responses do not expose page/size/totalPages metadata. Under the performance review standard, collection-returning APIs should use Pageable/Page-style contracts with default and max size.
findings.evidence: ProductRequestOptions.toPageable(...) returns PageRequest.of(0, safeLimit, toSort(sort)); AdminZeroHitController also exposes only limit, and ZeroHitQueryService calls PageRequest.of(0, resolvedLimit, resolvedSort).
findings.suggestedFix: Add a validated page parameter, build PageRequest.of(page, safeSize, sort), and return pagination metadata such as page, size, totalElements, and totalPages for list/search/dashboard collection responses.

findings.title: Zero-hit dashboard scans the same filtered range three times for summary metrics
findings.description: listZeroHits runs countRadarItems, sumHitCount, and sumEstimatedOpportunityLoss as three separate aggregate queries over the same since predicate. This is avoidable DB work on every dashboard request.
findings.evidence:
ZeroHitSummaryDto summary = new ZeroHitSummaryDto(
    zeroHitSearchRepository.countRadarItems(since),
    zeroHitSearchRepository.sumHitCount(since),
    zeroHitSearchRepository.sumEstimatedOpportunityLoss(since));
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the three repository methods with one projection query, for example select new com.skishop.dto.ZeroHitSummaryDto(count(z), coalesce(sum(z.hitCount), 0), coalesce(sum(z.estimatedOpportunityLoss), 0)) from ZeroHitSearch z where z.lastSearchedAt >= :since.

findings.title: Product keyword search is non-sargable and existing indexes will not help contains matching
findings.description: The search specification applies lower(column) LIKE '%keyword%' across manufacturer, name, category, and description. Leading wildcards plus lower() prevent normal B-tree index use; the migration creates plain indexes on name/manufacturer/category, not functional or trigram indexes. This will become a sequential-scan search as product volume grows.
findings.evidence: String pattern = "%" + keyword.trim().toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) + "%"; criteriaBuilder.like(criteriaBuilder.lower(root.get("manufacturer")), pattern) ... description. Migration V1 creates CREATE INDEX idx_products_name_lower ON products (name), not lower(name) or gin_trgm_ops.
findings.suggestedFix: For PostgreSQL, use pg_trgm GIN indexes on lower(name), lower(manufacturer), lower(category), and lower(description), or move product search to full-text search. Validate with EXPLAIN ANALYZE before changing query strategy.

findings.title: Stable product context is queried on every AI consultation without caching
findings.description: AI consultation fetches distinct categories and manufacturers every request. These are product-master values seeded by Flyway and appear infrequently changing, making them good candidates for Spring Cache. Without caching, each AI consult adds two DB round trips before the AI call/fallback path.
findings.evidence: new AiPromptContext(productRepository.findDistinctCategories(), productRepository.findDistinctManufacturers())
findings.suggestedFix: Add a small read-through cache around product prompt context, for example @Cacheable on a ProductContextService method. If product admin mutations are added later, pair it with @CacheEvict on writes.

escalations.description: Confirm whether product and zero-hit collection endpoints are intentionally first-window only for the MVP, or whether OSS quality requires navigable pagination now. The performance recommendation is to add page metadata, but this is an API contract decision.

| 3 | High | Pagination | src/main/java/com/skishop/service/ProductRequestOptions.java | 34 | PageRequest.of(0, ...) creates a first-page-only API. Collection endpoints expose limit but not page/size/totalPages metadata. | Add validated page parameters and return page metadata. |
| 4 | Medium | JPA query optimization | src/main/java/com/skishop/service/ZeroHitQueryService.java | 64 | Dashboard summary performs three aggregate queries over the same since predicate. | Use one summary projection query returning count, sum(hitCount), and sum(estimatedOpportunityLoss). |
| 5 | Medium | Query shape / indexing | src/main/java/com/skishop/service/ProductSpecifications.java | 39 | lower(column) LIKE '%keyword%' cannot use the current plain B-tree indexes for contains search. | Use PostgreSQL full-text search or pg_trgm GIN functional indexes, verified with EXPLAIN ANALYZE. |
| 6 | Medium | Cache strategy | src/main/java/com/skishop/service/AiConsultationService.java | 45 | AI prompt context runs distinct category and manufacturer queries on every consultation. | Cache the stable product context with Spring Cache and add eviction when product writes exist. |

## Scorecard
| Evaluation Item | Score (1-5) | Notes |
|-----------------|-------------|-------|
| N+1 Query Prevention | 5/5 | No relationships or DB calls inside production loops found. |
| JPA Query Optimization | 2/5 | Duplicate count queries, repeated aggregates, and non-sargable search need cleanup. |
| Pagination | 2/5 | Limits are capped, but APIs are first-page-only and lack page metadata. |
| Memory Efficiency | 4/5 | Bounded result sizes and Java records are good; entity materialization remains acceptable for current DTO shape. |
| Cache Strategy | 3/5 | No cache for stable product master context used by AI consult. |
| **Overall Score** | **16/25** | Main risks are DB query count and scalable collection/search behavior. |

## Escalation Items (Requires Human Judgment)
- Decide whether collection APIs are intentionally first-window only for the MVP, or whether public OSS quality requires navigable pagination in the current API contract.

results.summary: Resilience review found one critical gap and several high/medium risks around the live Spring AI external call. Actuator health probes are enabled and no direct RestTemplate instantiation was found, but the AI provider path lacks retry/circuit breaker, explicit timeout, bulkhead isolation, and graceful shutdown settings.

findings.title: Live AI provider call has no retry or circuit breaker protection
findings.description: SpringAiProviderClient performs the external AI call directly through ChatClient without @Retry, @CircuitBreaker, or equivalent Spring Retry/Resilience4j wrapper. If the provider is intermittently failing, the first failure reaches the service path immediately and there is no circuit breaker to stop repeated calls during an outage.
findings.evidence: generate() calls chatClient.prompt(prompt).call().content() at line 35. Repository-wide search found no @Retry, @CircuitBreaker, @TimeLimiter, @Bulkhead, resilience4j configuration, or Spring Retry usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add Resilience4j Spring Boot support and wrap the provider call, for example @Retry(name = "aiProvider", fallbackMethod = "fallback") and @CircuitBreaker(name = "aiProvider", fallbackMethod = "fallback"), with YAML config using maxAttempts 3, exponential backoff, and a bounded open-state wait. Ensure the fallback returns Optional.empty() or throws AiProviderException consistently so AiConsultationService keeps returning FALLBACK/ERROR responses.

findings.title: External AI call has no explicit connect/read or operation timeout
findings.description: The OpenAI-compatible Spring AI client is built without any visible timeout configuration. A slow or stalled provider can therefore hold a request thread until lower-level defaults apply, which is unsafe for an admin API backed by an external service.
findings.evidence: OpenAiApi.builder() only sets apiKey, and OpenAiChatModel only sets model options. application.yml also has no Spring AI/OpenAI timeout or Resilience4j TimeLimiter settings.
findings.suggestedFix: Configure explicit provider timeouts through the supported Spring AI/OpenAI client builder or properties, and add an overall operation timeout. Target values should be short and documented, for example connect timeout 3-5s and read/operation timeout 10-20s for this admin consultation endpoint.

findings.title: Graceful shutdown is not configured
findings.description: The server configuration does not enable graceful shutdown or a per-phase shutdown timeout. During deployments or container restarts, in-flight admin/API requests may be interrupted instead of drained.
findings.evidence: The server block configures request/header/error limits but does not include server.shutdown=graceful or spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `server.shutdown: graceful` and `spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase: 20s` or another bounded value aligned with deployment probe/drain settings.

findings.title: No custom health/readiness signal exists for the AI provider dependency
findings.description: Actuator health probes are enabled, but there is no HealthIndicator for the live AI provider. If live AI is considered operationally important, /actuator/health/readiness will not expose provider degradation or support targeted alerting.
findings.evidence: management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled is true and health is exposed, but repository-wide search found no HealthIndicator implementation. The only live external provider path is SpringAiProviderClient.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a custom AI provider HealthIndicator or readiness group member. If AI is intentionally optional because fallback is acceptable, document that decision and expose a non-gating indicator or metric so operations can still detect provider outages.

findings.title: Live AI calls have no concurrency isolation
findings.description: The AI provider call runs in the request path without a bulkhead or concurrency limit. Under provider slowness, many admin requests can occupy servlet threads and degrade unrelated backend endpoints.
findings.evidence: The provider call is synchronous and repository-wide search found no @Bulkhead or equivalent isolation around the AI provider path.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a Resilience4j semaphore bulkhead for the AI provider, sized to expected admin concurrency. Combine it with timeout and circuit breaker settings so queued or saturated calls degrade to the existing fallback/error response path.

escalations.description: Decide whether live AI availability should gate readiness. The application has a user-facing fallback, so making AI readiness non-gating may be correct, but operations still need visibility into provider outages.
